Faculty/Department-Level Unit: Dean-Med-Centre for Sustainable Medicine

Employee Category: Research Staff

Location\\_ONB: Kent Ridge Campus

Posting Start Date: 13/02/2026

**Job Description**
-------------------

Climate change is the defining challenge of this century, and healthcare is both a victim of climate change and a major contributor to it. The Centre for Sustainable Medicine (CoSM) at the National University of Singapore works at the frontier of policy, clinical systems, and global health to accelerate the transition to low-carbon, climate-resilient health systems across Asia and worldwide.

**Purpose of the Post**

We invite applications for a senior leader in the field of healthcare system sustainability, to lead and grow the Centre’s work on mitigation and adaptation efforts and the health facility level.

The postholder will be responsible for taking CoSM’s world-leading work on preparing climate-smart health systems, hospitals, and clinical pathways, looking to integrate both mitigation and adaptation approaches.

This is a **globally outward-facing role** involving regular international engagement and travel, and combining applied policy work, academic research, and real-world implementation. The Centre is open to applications from experts from a wide range of seniority, spanning Post-Doctoral Research Fellows through to Research Associate Professors.

**Key Responsibilities include:**

* **Research Leadership in Health System Sustainability**

* Develop, lead, and grow a coherent body of research on decarbonisation of the healthcare physical and built environment, including infrastructure, estates, energy use, procurement, and transport.

* Integrate climate adaptation and resilience solutions into decarbonisation and systems-level sustainability research.
* Deliver high-impact peer-reviewed publications, competitive grant applications, and multi-institution research collaborations at regional and global levels.
* Work closely across the Centre’s research and policy and implementation teams to ensure this thinking is embedded across research, from design through to real-world delivery.
  

**2. Policy Engagement and External Partnerships**

* Lead and contribute to major international projects across Asia-Pacific, and with global multilateral organisations, and national health systems.
* Translate research findings into policy briefs, technical guidance, and implementation frameworks for health system sustainability.
* Represent the Centre in international technical forums, expert groups, and advisory processes.
* Lead and develop individual and collaborative grant proposals to grow the capacity of the Centre and their own body of work.
  

**3. Education and Academic Programme Development**

* Design, convene, and deliver a number of postgraduate modules on climate change, sustainability, and health systems as part of the existing MSc and Executive Fellowship in Sustainable Healthcare.
* Lead the development of a new PhD Programme as part of the Centre’s work, and provide direct supervision to PhD and MSc students, including thesis supervision and examination.
* Oversee and provide strategic leadership for the Centre’s education portfolio, including curriculum development, quality assurance, administration, and pedagogical innovation.

**4. Contribution to the Centre, NUS Medicine, and the wider University**

* Contribute positively to the culture, cohesion, and collaborative spirit of the Centre and wider institution.
* Support interdisciplinary initiatives, mentoring of junior staff, and shared academic and administrative responsibilities.
* Actively participate in seminars, workshops, and outreach activities that enhance the Centre’s visibility and impact.

**Qualifications**
------------------

***Essential***

* PhD in Public Health, Environmental Health, Engineering, Climate Change, or an equivalent field.
* Strong academic publications and leadership of relevant research programmes.
* Strong track record in applying research methods to real-world policy situations.
* Excellent analytical, quantitative, and written communication skills.
* Ability to operate confidently in international, multidisciplinary, policy-facing environments.
  

***Highly desirable***

* Experience working with governments, multilateral organisations, or large health systems.
* Experience assessing the environmental sustainability of the built environment.
* Familiarity with climate, sustainability, or health system transformation agendas.
* Strong quantitative and modelling skills using tools such as R, Python, Stata, Excel, or similar.
  

Remuneration will be commensurate with the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Informal enquiries are welcome and should be made to Professor Nick Watts at n.watts@nus.edu.sg.

  

**Formal application**: Please submit your application, indicating current/expected salary, supported by a detailed CV (including personal particulars, academic and employment history, complete list of publications/oral presentations and full contacts of three (3) referees to this job portal. We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

**More Information**
--------------------

The Environmental Monitoring & Modelling Division (EMMD) oversees and manages a comprehensive air and water quality monitoring programme to ensure that effective monitoring of the air and water quality and enable policies to be formulated to improve air and water quality. You will be part of the Environmental Quality Monitoring Department (EQMD) in EMMD which will be using the air and water quality data collected to analyse and identify anomalies, assess long-term trends, and inform policies for the improvement of air and water quality. * Formulate, review, and implement ambient air quality monitoring programmes for assessment of environmental quality and to ensure that the programmes are carried out effectively

* Plan and conduct air quality research studies, and foster collaborative relationships with academia, research institutes, and international organisations to drive impactful research that strengthens pollution control operations
* Provide technical and scientific advice on air quality monitoring and environmental impact assessments to internal and external stakeholders
* Prepare project proposals, technical reports and research manuscripts, and present findings to senior management and at local and international meetings and conferences
* Respond to media and public queries on air quality issues including haze episodes
* Participate actively in cross-functional project teams, inter-agency meetings, and working groups to support environmental management efforts

**[What we are looking for]**

* Degree in Environmental Science, Chemistry, or other fields related to air quality monitoring and assessment
* Knowledge in air quality sampling and analysis, air pollution sources and characteristics, air quality research, data analytics, and/or statistics (e.g. R) would be an advantage
* Driven, self-motivated and resourceful
* Demonstrate critical and analytical thinking and ability to articulate views clearly
* Good communication and presentation skills, with good command of spoken and written English
* Demonstrate ability to undertake work both individually and part of a team

We’re looking for an Environmental Engineer Level I to join our Singapore team.

When you work for us, you get the chance to join nearly 50,000 people all driven by a common purpose of delivering a more sustainable world. We’re excited about the challenges ahead. We believe there’s never been a more rewarding time to work in the energy, chemical and resources sectors.

We are seeking an **environmental professional with a strong background in biodiversity,** preferably **marine and coastal ecosystems,** to join our growing environmental consulting team in Singapore. This role is suited for a technically strong individual who enjoys applied, project-based work and contributing to environmental assessments, monitoring programmes, and advisory projects across marine and coastal environments.

As an Environmental Engineer Level I you will be responsible for primarily supporting **marine biodiversity studies,** including baseline surveys, impact assessments, and environmental management planning, with opportunities to work across multidisciplinary environmental projects.

To succeed in this role, you should have experience in **project coordination or task-level project management** is advantageous but not mandatory.

**Who we are**

Worley is a global professional services company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia.

Right now, we’re bridging two worlds as we accelerate to more sustainable energy sources, while helping our customers provide the energy, chemicals and resources that society needs now.

We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value over the life of their portfolio of assets. We solve complex problems by finding integrated data-centric solutions from the first stages of consulting and engineering to installation and commissioning, to the last stages of decommissioning and remediation. Join us and help drive innovation and sustainability in our projects.

**What you’ll do**

We are looking for an **Environmental Engineer Level I** to join our team in **Singapore.**

The role responsibilities include:

* Contribute to marine and coastal EIA and EMMP projects, including baseline ecological surveys, impact assessments, and monitoring programmes.
* Support and prepare inputs for Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA), Environmental Monitoring and Management Plans (EMMP),
* Environmental and Social Due Diligence (ESDD), and related environmental studies.
* Plan and participate in marine ecological and biodiversity field surveys, including data collection, species assessments, and habitat evaluations.
* Analyse and interpret ecological and environmental data, and contribute to clear, defensible technical conclusions.
* Prepare high-quality technical reports, figures, tables, and presentations for clients and regulators.
* Participate in client meetings, providing technical input and practical, science-based recommendations.
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary project teams under defined timelines and budgets.
* Where applicable, support project coordination activities, such as task planning, scheduling, fieldwork logistics, and progress tracking.
* Contribute to maintaining a safe and healthy workplace, including adherence to fieldwork and HSE requirements.

**What you’ll have**

* Degree in Environmental Science, Marine Biology, Ecology, Environmental Management, or a related discipline from a recognized university.
* Strong foundation in marine biodiversity and ecology, including habitats, species, and ecological processes.
* Experience in marine or coastal ecological field surveys, with understanding of survey methods, best practices, and relevant guidelines.
* Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within project teams.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly for technical reporting.
* Candidates with Singapore or regional environmental experience will be favorably considered.
* Ability to obtain and maintain clearance to work in secure areas in Singapore, where required.
* Familiarity with environmental data analysis tools or GIS (e.g. QGIS, ArcGIS).
* Experience in project management will be viewed favourably.

**Moving forward together**

We want our people to be energized and empowered to drive sustainable impact. So, our focus is on a values-inspired culture that unlocks brilliance through belonging, connection and innovation.

We’re building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. Creating a space where everyone feels they belong, can be themselves, and are heard.

And we're not just talking about it; we're doing it. We're reskilling our people, leveraging transferable skills, and supporting the transition of our workforce to become experts in today's low carbon energy infrastructure and technology.

Whatever your ambition, there’s a path for you here. And there’s no barrier to your potential career success. Join us to broaden your horizons, explore diverse opportunities, and be part of delivering sustainable change.
